OpenSSF Best Practices Silver gaps

This page compares every criterion for the OpenSSF Best Practices Silver badge with this repository, and names either the evidence that already satisfies it or what is still missing. It is the repository-side answer sheet: the badge form itself still needs the Silver-only answers, justifications, and URLs entered at the project page.

Checked on 2026-11-01 against origin/main at commit 435a5c15.

Sources

  • Criteria: all levels and Silver only. The Silver page lists 55 active criteria: 44 MUST, 10 SHOULD, and 1 SUGGESTED, which matches criteria statistics and the categories in criteria.yml.
  • Badge state: the project JSON at bestpractices.dev/projects/16161.json reports badge_level: "passing" and achieve_silver_status: "Unmet".
  • Scoring: the badge awards a level only at 100% of that level's active criteria. A Met or N/A answer with the required justification counts; a partial answer does not. Silver therefore needs all 55, not a subset.

How to read the states

State Meaning
Met The repository has the required artefact, workflow, or documented process.
Partial Something real exists, but it does not yet satisfy the whole criterion.
Gap Nothing in the repository satisfies the criterion.
N/A The criterion does not apply to this project; the badge form needs the N/A answer with this justification.

The project holds the Passing badge: its 67 active criteria are answered, with 60 Met and 7 N/A, and none Unmet. Seven of the 55 Silver criteria are also Passing criteria, so their answers carry over: contribution_requirements, report_tracker, tests_documented_added, warnings_strict, crypto_weaknesses, static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities (all Met), and dynamic_analysis_unsafe (N/A). achieve_passing is also already Met. The remaining 47 Silver-only criteria have no answer yet.

Where the project stands

Count
Silver criteria 55

Basics

Criterion Level State Evidence in this repository What closes a gap
achieve_passing MUST Met The badge JSON reports badge_level: "passing" and achieve_passing_status: "Met"; README.md links project 16161 in the badge row. —
contribution_requirements MUST Met CONTRIBUTING.md states the coding standard, test requirement, static analysis, build, and security rules; Pull requests states the review and evidence expectations. Also answered at Passing. —
dco SHOULD Gap No DCO or CLA: nothing in CONTRIBUTING.md asks for Signed-off-by, there is no DCO file or workflow, and the last 200 commits contain no sign-off. The Apache-2.0 sentence is a licence grant, not a per-contribution legal assertion. Add a DCO, require the sign-off in CONTRIBUTING and CI, and link the DCO.
governance MUST Met GOVERNANCE.md defines the roles, decision process, decision records, escalation path, ownership transfer, and how the document changes. —
code_of_conduct MUST Met CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md is at the repository root and linked for enforcement from GOVERNANCE.md. —
roles_responsibilities MUST Met GOVERNANCE.md has the role table; MAINTAINERS.md names the maintainer and every detector owner; CODEOWNERS routes review for owned paths. —
access_continuity MUST Gap One maintainer is named in MAINTAINERS.md. No continuity plan, backup account access, or second person is documented who could create issues, merge, and release within a week. When an owner steps away covers detector ownership only. Document a continuity plan for accounts, keys, and releases, and test it with a release cut by a second person.
bus_factor SHOULD Gap The maintainer table has one person, and review expectations escalate to the same person. Add a second maintainer with merge and release rights, recorded in GOVERNANCE, MAINTAINERS, and CODEOWNERS.
documentation_roadmap MUST Partial docs/ROADMAP.md is dated 2026-10-15 → 2027-04-15, about six months, plus “After v1 — Future” and “Not in this roadmap”. Extend the dated roadmap to at least 2027-11 and keep the explicit not-doing list.
documentation_architecture MUST Met docs/ARCHITECTURE.md has the layer diagram, owned boundaries, trust boundaries, and hosting model. —
documentation_security MUST Met SECURITY.md, docs/THREAT_MODEL.md, and docs/PRIVACY.md state what users can and cannot expect, including residual risk. —
documentation_quick_start MUST Met docs/QUICKSTART.md goes from the first scan to CI in five steps; README.md links the 90-second demo. —
documentation_current MUST Partial CI checks generated reference, Open Graph, answer, and llms-full pages in ci.yml; docs/generated-files.md inventories every generated output and its readers. The docs doctor job and the Seaworthy job in pages.yml run report-only (level: none, --fail-on none), so a known documentation defect does not fail review. Make a documentation defect check blocking, or track known defects to closure in one list.
documentation_achievements MUST Met The README.md badge row links the Best Practices project, Scorecard, npm, CI, CodeQL, and the other recognitions; SECURITY.md links the badge again. — (keep the badge within 48 hours of a new recognition)
accessibility_best_practices SHOULD Partial The Lighthouse job in pages.yml asserts accessibility ≥ 0.9 on the home page and one rule page of the Pages build artifact (config); BRAND_GUIDE.md records WCAG AA colour pairs. There is no accessibility statement, WCAG target, full-site audit, or CLI output audit. Publish an accessibility statement with a target, and audit every site template and the CLI output.
internationalization SHOULD Partial docs/i18n/fa/README.md and docs/i18n/fa/QUICKSTART.md are Persian translations, linked from the English README. CLI and documentation strings are English-only and have no message catalog. Decide the i18n scope, document it, and either add a message catalog or record why English-only is the deliberate choice.
sites_password_security MUST N/A The project site is a static GitHub Pages build of docs/ deployed from a workflow artifact (pages.yml, _config.yml); it has no accounts, authentication, or stored passwords. GitHub handles authentication for the repository. Enter N/A with this justification.

Change Control

Criterion Level State Evidence in this repository What closes a gap
maintenance_or_update MUST Partial Releases use SemVer and release notes (RELEASING.md), and COMPATIBILITY.md documents deprecation windows and notice periods. SECURITY.md supports security fixes for the latest release only, and there is no supported-version window or step-by-step upgrade guide for an older release. State a support window and publish an upgrade path for versions users are likely to still run.

Reporting

Criterion Level State Evidence in this repository What closes a gap
report_tracker MUST Met Public GitHub Issues with issue forms in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/; README and CONTRIBUTING link it. Also answered at Passing. —
vulnerability_report_credit MUST Met SECURITY.md says a published advisory credits the reporter unless they ask to stay anonymous. —
vulnerability_response_process MUST Met SECURITY.md documents private reporting, a seven-day acknowledgement, a 30-day assessment or fix plan, and an advisory with affected and fixed versions. —

Quality

Criterion Level State Evidence in this repository What closes a gap
coding_standards MUST Partial CONTRIBUTING.md names the TypeScript compiler flags (strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, exactOptionalPropertyTypes) and says to match the surrounding code. It does not name a style guide for formatting, naming, or imports. Name the style guide contributions must follow and document it in CONTRIBUTING.
coding_standards_enforced MUST Gap npm run check is the TypeScript build, the Action bundle, the test suite, plugin drift, and the plugin evals (package.json, check-pipeline.ts). There is no ESLint, Prettier, Biome, or other formatter/linter configuration or CI step, so type checking is the only automated enforcement. Add a FLOSS formatter and linter to npm run check and CI.
build_standard_variables MUST N/A The project produces no native binaries; it compiles TypeScript with tsc and bundles the Action with ncc. No C/C++ compiler or linker step exists to pass CC, CFLAGS, or LDFLAGS to. Enter N/A with this justification.
build_preserve_debug SHOULD N/A There is no end-user build or install system with debug flags: npm ships the compiled package, and the files list excludes source maps. Enter N/A with this justification.
build_non_recursive MUST N/A The build is one tsc -b project plus an ncc bundle; there is no recursive native build over cross-dependent subdirectories. Enter N/A with this justification.
build_repeatable MUST Met npm run check:reproducible builds twice and compares npm tarballs byte for byte; it is a release gate in RELEASING.md and the release workflow. CI also records the tarball hash on Linux, Windows, and macOS and fails ci-ok when the runners disagree, which catches a build step that depends on the host. The data bundle is likewise built twice and must be identical. —
installation_common MUST Met npm install and npm uninstall through the published package, with bin entries in package.json; docs/INSTALL.md documents it. —
installation_standard_variables MUST N/A npm owns the install location and prefix; the project ships no installer that writes artifacts into POSIX paths or should honour DESTDIR. Enter N/A with this justification.
installation_development_quick MUST Met CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md both give git clone, npm ci, npm run check; the repository also has a Codespaces/dev-container path. —
external_dependencies MUST Met package.json declares dependencies and package-lock.json pins them; GitHub Actions are pinned to full SHAs; signed data bundles list every file with a digest. —
dependency_monitoring MUST Met dependabot.yml updates npm and Actions weekly; the self-scan job in ci.yml scans this repository on every push to main and in the merge queue and fails on findings outside the baseline; scorecard.yml runs weekly. —
updateable_reused_components MUST Met The lockfile, Dependabot update groups with a cooldown, SHA-pinned Actions, and npm ci make a reused component a one-line update. —
interfaces_current SHOULD Met The self-scan job fails on findings outside the baseline on every push to main and every merge-queue run; AGENTS.md requires offing check before adding a dependency or Action, and the opt-in pre-push hook runs the same gate locally; COMPATIBILITY.md states when an interface is deprecated. —
automated_integration_testing MUST Met ci.yml runs the suite on every push to main, every merge-queue run, and every pull request except a docs-only change; npm run check runs the 420 test files under tests/, and the jobs report pass/fail. —
regression_tests_added50 MUST Partial CONTRIBUTING.md and the pull request template require a test with a bug fix, and the coverage floors keep tests growing. Nothing measures the share of the last six months' bug fixes that actually shipped a regression test. Measure and report the ratio, or automate a check that every fix: change adds a test.
test_statement_coverage80 MUST Met test:coverage in package.json enforces 93% lines, 87% branches, and 93% functions; ci.yml runs it on main and uploads LCOV. —
test_policy_mandated MUST Met CONTRIBUTING.md and Quality standards require a test for new functionality and bug fixes; AGENTS.md step 4 repeats it. —
tests_documented_added MUST Met CONTRIBUTING.md and the pull request template's “Tests added or updated” checkbox document the requirement for change proposals. —
warnings_strict MUST Met Already answered Met at Passing. tsconfig.json enables strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, and exactOptionalPropertyTypes, and the build fails on every compiler error, so type-level warnings are strict. There is no linter, so a linter with strict warning rules would strengthen the answer but is not needed to keep this criterion Met. — (optional: add the strict linter from the style-enforcement gap)

Security

Criterion Level State Evidence in this repository What closes a gap
implement_secure_design MUST Met docs/THREAT_MODEL.md applies STRIDE to each surface with mitigations and residual risk; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md records the boundaries; repository and registry content are treated as data and never executed. —
crypto_weaknesses MUST Met The only hash the product computes is SHA-256 (createHash("sha256") in scan-cache.ts, data-bundle.ts, baseline.ts, reporters.ts, and treemap.ts); no MD5 or SHA-1 appears in src/. Signature checks use Sigstore. —
crypto_algorithm_agility SHOULD N/A The project implements no cryptographic algorithms and exposes no algorithm choice; signing and verification are delegated to Sigstore, and transport security to Node TLS. Enter N/A with this justification.
crypto_credential_agility MUST N/A Offing stores no authentication credentials or private keys. The GitHub token is read per run from the action input or environment, and the Sigstore trusted root is public data shipped in the package. Enter N/A with this justification.
crypto_used_network SHOULD Met Every network path is HTTPS: signed data releases, the optional GitHub API comment, and the user's own package install (PRIVACY.md). There is no FTP, plain HTTP, or other insecure transport. —
crypto_tls12 SHOULD Met All TLS goes through Node's fetch/undici, which requires TLS 1.2 or newer by default; no custom TLS version or cipher configuration exists in src/. —
crypto_certificate_verification MUST Met No rejectUnauthorized: false, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, or plain-HTTP fallback appears in src/; certificate verification stays at the Node default. —
crypto_verification_private MUST Met The only private value sent over the network is the GitHub token in a request header, and it goes through fetch only after the TLS handshake, with no plain-HTTP path (pr-comment.ts, action-fix-pr.ts). —
signed_releases MUST Met The release publish stages (release-publish-binaries.yml, release-publish-container.yml) sign binaries and checksums with keyless Sigstore, add a build-provenance attestation and SLSA provenance, and sign the image digest too; release.yml publishes npm with --provenance. RELEASING.md documents the public verification commands. Keys are short-lived OIDC identities, never stored on the distribution site. —
version_tags_signed SUGGESTED Gap Tags are annotated but unsigned: RELEASING.md tells maintainers to run git tag -a, and release.yml moves the major tag with git tag --force. No -s/-u and no published key or verification instructions exist. Sign release and major tags with a published key and document verification.
input_validation MUST Met Zod schemas validate MCP tool input and capabilities (mcp.ts, capabilities.ts); validateRegistryV2 validates every registry before rules are used (registry.ts); published JSON Schemas live in schemas/; THREAT_MODEL.md records the file-size, nesting, and symlink limits. —
hardening SHOULD Met The product is memory-safe TypeScript with strict null and index checks, parsers have byte and time budgets, JSON depth is capped, and untrusted text is never evaluated as code. THREAT_MODEL.md lists these controls. The vendored tree-sitter runtime evaluates its own generated WebAssembly glue, not repository text (tree-sitter.cjs). —
assurance_case MUST Partial docs/THREAT_MODEL.md has the threat model, trust boundaries, per-surface threats, mitigations, and residual risk. It is not framed as an assurance case and does not argue secure design principles or common implementation weakness classes against stated security requirements. Add docs/ASSURANCE_CASE.md that ties the requirements in SECURITY.md to threats, controls, and evidence.

Analysis

Criterion Level State Evidence in this repository What closes a gap
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities MUST Met codeql.yml runs CodeQL for JavaScript and TypeScript weekly and on demand and uploads SARIF; scorecard.yml and the dogfood Offing Action in ci.yml upload their SARIF to the same code-scanning dashboard. Already answered Met at Passing. —
dynamic_analysis_unsafe MUST N/A No memory-unsafe language is produced: the package is TypeScript/JavaScript, no C or C++ is built, and the tree-sitter runtime is a prebuilt WebAssembly dependency. Already answered N/A at Passing. Enter N/A with this justification.

Gaps to file

The issue that requested this page says to open one issue per real gap. This session was limited to pull requests, so no issues were opened; the titles below are ready to file as they are. One row can close more than one criterion when the underlying fix is the same.

# Criteria Ready-to-file issue title
1 dco Add a DCO sign-off requirement for contributions
2 access_continuity, bus_factor Document a continuity plan and add a second maintainer with release access
3 documentation_roadmap Extend the roadmap to cover at least the next twelve months
4 documentation_current Make documentation defect checks blocking and track known defects
5 accessibility_best_practices Publish an accessibility statement and audit the site and CLI
6 internationalization Decide and document the internationalization scope for docs and CLI output
7 maintenance_or_update Publish a supported-version and upgrade policy for older releases
8 coding_standards, coding_standards_enforced Name a coding style guide and enforce it with a linter and formatter
9 regression_tests_added50 Measure and report regression tests added for fixed bugs
10 assurance_case Add an assurance case for the security requirements
11 version_tags_signed Sign release tags and document how to verify them

What the badge form still needs

The 47 unanswered Silver-only criteria need a status plus the justification or URL the form requires; the N/A criteria also need the justification shown above. Reviewing the seven shared answers and achieve_passing before submitting is cheap, and the evidence column in this page names the file or workflow to cite for every criterion.
